title: Urgent item
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.3, #773; P25 live alarms: #775), not implemented. One item of the urgent lane as capture sends it to the hub in `POST /api/station/urgent` (capture-urgent-request.schema.json): an emergency alarm or a change of a live page, with its age at the moment of sending. Every key is required and none is null. On the hub its identity is (station, key, rev). `age_s` is measured on CLOCK_BOOTTIME (`age_src` `boot`); an item from before a reboot has no boot-clock age and is sent with the wall-clock age `now - event_at`, clamped at 0 (`age_src` `wall`): it is never held back and `age_s` is never null. An alarm's age is never the larger of two clocks, and capture never expires an alarm. A page's clock runs per revision: a revision unsent 120 s after capture made it (the larger of its two ages; exactly 120 s is expired) is not sent, except an `ended` one, which stays sendable for 10 min. `$defs/held` is the same item as capture holds it and hands it to the app; `$defs/data` is the `data` column of the urgent file's row (contracts/capture/urgent.sql).

key.description: The item's idempotency key, 1 to 200 characters. An analog alarm raised live: `<channel label without spaces>-live-<int(carrier start * 1000)>`. An analog alarm found at the close: the transmission's own item id. A P25 live alarm (#775): `p25-<system>-<talkgroup>-<radio id>-<int(event_at * 1000)>`, the grant's own time; capture's `at` only when the grant carries none (`data.key_time`). A page: `page:<channel>:<started, 2 decimals>`. Not station-qualified: on the hub an item is (station, key, rev), the station from the token.

rev.description: The revision of the item under its key: always 0 for an alarm; for a page 0, 1, 2, ... one per change of the page. On the station an item's identity is (key, rev).

kind.description: What the item is. The hub answers an unknown kind `rejected` (reason `kind`) and takes the rest of the request.

at.description: When capture made the item, Unix seconds (the station's wall clock). Set once: the same value in the row, in every frame and in every request that carries the item.

event_at.description: When it happened on the air, Unix seconds (the station's wall clock): the carrier's start for an alarm raised live, the grant's time for a P25 alarm, the first tone's start for a page. The hub never places the item by this: it uses its own clock minus `age_s`.

age_s.description: The item's age when this request was made, seconds, at least 0, never null: the sender's CLOCK_BOOTTIME minus the item's `event_boot` when both are of one boot, else its wall clock minus `event_at`, clamped at 0. The hub places the item at its own now minus this; it clamps a value over 24 h.

age_src.description: The clock `age_s` was measured on: `boot`, or `wall` for an item from before a reboot. The hub cannot check or correct a wall-sourced age (two readings of the station's one clock): it takes it as given, bounded, and labels the alarm's age as approximate. A hub takes a word it does not know as `wall`.

data.title: The item's data
data.description: What the item says: the `data` column of the urgent file's row, as an object. An alarm carries the alarm keys, a page the page keys; which are required follows `kind` (`$defs/by-kind`). The keys of every kind are typed here in one object, so a kind added later must not reuse one of these names with another type. No rig (the hub derives it), no audio, no transcript, no secret.

source.description: An alarm: the channel's label. A P25 alarm: the name the finished call's row will carry as its source, so the hub's same-radio rule sees one channel.

start.description: An alarm: the carrier's (or the grant's) start, Unix seconds.

end.description: An alarm: when the transmission ended, Unix seconds. Optional: an alarm raised at the key-up has none yet.

radio_id.description: An alarm: the id of the radio whose button it was, digits as a string (several: joined with `, `, as today).

ids.description: An alarm: the radio ids decoded so far, as the sidecar's `ids`.

unit.description: An alarm: the radio's alias from the wish's `aliases` map; "" when it has none.

emergency_via.description: An alarm: the signalling the button came in.

system.description: A P25 alarm (#775): the system's short name.

talkgroup.description: A P25 alarm (#775): the talkgroup number.

key_time.description: A P25 live alarm (#775): which time its key was made from. `grant`: the grant's own time as trunk-recorder stamps it (`event_at`), so one grant on one station always gives one key; `capture`: capture's `at`, only when the grant carried no time.

trimmed.description: Either kind: the item was over the request's 65,536 bytes on its own and was sent with its `data` cut to the essentials (an alarm: no `ids`, each string at most 200 characters; a page: as many `pairs` as fit). The row keeps the full `data` and the app's lane carries it whole. Default false; a trimmed item still has every required field.

channel.description: A page: the paging channel's label.

started.description: A page: when the first tone started, Unix seconds.

pairs.description: A page: the tone pairs decoded so far, in order.

phase.description: A page: `tones` while pairs are still coming, `voice` once the dispatcher speaks.

ours.description: A page: any pair is ours.

ended.description: A page: the page is over.

until.description: A page: the station's wall-clock time until which an ended page is still shown, Unix seconds; null while it goes out. The hub's expiry for its live entry.

pair.title: One tone pair
pair.description: One A/B tone pair of a page, as the live decode shows it.

names.description: Who this pair pages, by name (the wish's tone plan); [] for a pair the station does not know.

ours.description: The pair pages one of this department's own.

at.description: When the pair was certain, Unix seconds.

by-kind.title: What each kind requires
by-kind.description: The keys of `data` a reader may rely on, by `kind`. An item of a kind this schema does not know needs only the envelope.

rev.description: An alarm has one revision, 0: its key alone is its identity.

data.description: An alarm's data: what a reader may rely on.
A page's data: what a reader may rely on.

held.title: An urgent item as capture holds it
held.description: The item with the columns of its row in the urgent file, as capture hands it to the app: in an `urgent` frame, and in the `rows` and `memory` of an `urgent_since` reply (capture-socket-event.schema.json, capture-socket-reply.schema.json). The app takes an item over once, by (key, rev), whichever way it arrives.

n.description: The item's row number in the urgent file: its place there and nothing else; the app's cursor is (urgent_epoch, n). null exactly while the item has no row (`durable` false).

key.description: The item's idempotency key, 1 to 200 characters. An analog alarm raised live: `<channel label without spaces>-live-<int(carrier start * 1000)>`. An analog alarm found at the close: the transmission's own item id. A P25 live alarm (#775): `p25-<system>-<talkgroup>-<radio id>-<int(event_at * 1000)>`, the grant's own time; capture's `at` only when the grant carries none (`data.key_time`). A page: `page:<channel>:<started, 2 decimals>`. Not station-qualified: on the hub an item is (station, key, rev), the station from the token.

rev.description: The revision of the item under its key: always 0 for an alarm; for a page 0, 1, 2, ... one per change of the page. On the station an item's identity is (key, rev).

kind.description: What the item is. A reader leaves an unknown kind alone.

at.description: When capture made the item, Unix seconds (the station's wall clock). Set once: the same value in the row, in every frame and in every request that carries the item.

event_at.description: When it happened on the air, Unix seconds (the station's wall clock): the carrier's start for an alarm raised live, the grant's time for a P25 alarm, the first tone's start for a page. The hub never places the item by this: it uses its own clock minus `age_s`.

event_boot.description: The same moment as `event_at` on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, seconds since boot `boot`.

boot.description: The boot id `event_boot` belongs to. Opaque: compared for equality only.

durable.description: The item has a row, committed and fsync'd. false: it lives in capture's memory only (a failed insert, a stalled disk) and `n` is null; when its row is written a second frame for the same (key, rev) follows with its `n` and `durable` true.
